repos.readme_excerpt:
# Battery-Emulator ⚡🔋

# What is Battery Emulator?

Many manufacturers sell home battery systems to enable homeowners to store power collected from the grid, or renewable sources, to use at times when electricity demand is higher. However almost all of these home battery systems charge a high cost for every kilowatt hour (kWh) of capacity you buy.

At the same time, EV manufacturers have been putting high capacity battery packs into their cars, with no firm plan for what should happen to those batteries if the car is damaged in a crash, or reaches the end of its life as a vehicle.

Battery Emulator enables EV battery packs to be repurposed for stationary storage. It acts as a translation layer between the EV battery and the home inverter. This makes it extremely cheap and easy to use large EV batteries in a true plug'n'play fashion!

repos.readme_excerpt:
An ultra lightweight macOS system monitor.

AirStats is a system monitor for the Mac menu bar. It reads CPU, memory, GPU, network, disk, battery, temperature, process and host statistics from the kernel and shows them in three places: the menu bar itself, a panel that drops down when you click the status item, and a desktop widget you can leave on screen.

It is built to be genuinely light. A menu bar monitor runs all day, every day, so AirStats holds a few megabytes and a fraction of a percent of one core rather than the tens of megabytes its peers take. It has no Dock icon, and reads the system through Mach, IOKit,

# Requirements

• macOS 14 or later

• Intel or Apple silicon

# Install

Download it from airstats.app, open the dmg and drag the app to Applications. The release includes both Intel (x86_64) and Apple silicon (arm64) builds in one app. It is signed and notarized, so it opens with no warning.

Describe a materials research task. MatOS assembles the scientific assets it needs, runs them as a stateful, checkable workflow, and turns every run into better assets for the next one.

# Contents

• What's in This Edition

# What is MatOS?

MatOS is an agent operating system for materials research. Materials studies run for days, cross literature, computation and experiment, and keep changing as results arrive. Agents for this work have to take on new data and software, keep long tasks on track, and remember what earlier tasks taught them. MatOS builds these capabilities around versioned scientific assets: data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles and workflows.

Research tasks drive the stateful adaptive workflow, the layered scientific asset graph supplies composable capabilities, and execution traces and user feedback become reviewed asset revisions that return to the graph.
